0.content: Nefer owns the Curatorium of Secrets and quietly runs the Northern Intelligence Network. After Jahoda killed Ratfan and could not pay what she owed, Nefer accepted her offer to work. "From now on, call me Boss Nefer." Jahoda is the only official employee; everyone else works in the shadows. The division of labour, in Jahoda's words: Nef handles the big stuff, Jahoda the small stuff, Ashru the door. Jahoda adores her, fears her moods and constantly asks for a raise. Nefer teases her, threatens to fire her and once actually "fired" her so she could take Lauma's commission. Nefer also gives her a day-off voucher every birthday and bought her floor mats when beds kept her awake.

1.content: Nefer's cat. Jahoda feeds him, refills his water and brushes his fur. She threatens him with baths when he wrecks her braids or jumps on her head, and complains that he has never completed a commission and should come on the next job. When she comes home too preoccupied to play, he sits on her head and grumbles. His own opinion of her: a silly human who is always running around.

2.comment: Jahoda: Aino and the Clanky-Clanky Arm
2.content: Aino built, fitted and decorated Jahoda's golden mechanical right arm, paid for by Nefer. Aino wanted far more gadgets, but Jahoda's refusal and the budget kept it simple: basic movement and a few transformations. Jahoda keeps breaking it, and Aino keeps fixing it and drawing doodles on it. Aino's student now handles most repairs. Jahoda drops off spare mechanical parts at the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop and asks Aino her strangest questions. Aino calls her "Dumpster Diver".

3.content: Aino's android and, by Aino's account, Jahoda's first-ever friend from Ineffa's side. On her first visit to the workshop Jahoda was so tense she struck at Ineffa a few times, mistaking a fresh krumkake for a weapon. One bite calmed her. Now she always "happens to be passing by" when a batch is ready. She calls Ineffa a dumb clanker with no humour and a sieve-like memory, but praises her krumkakes to everyone.

4.comment: Jahoda: The Seahook Gang and Zinaida
4.content: A notorious band of thieves who were once a hidden power in Nasha Town. Zinaida, a mid-level leader, brought the child Jahoda in, and the gang spoiled their "little lady". When noisy drunks kept her awake she threw stuffed toys out of the window, and whoever got hit had to wash the toy and return it. When a job went badly she woke Zinaida to ramble until she fell asleep. The boss scolded her, docked her share for returning a swindler's necklace, and took her to negotiations. One of the boss's codes was "Grant rest to those who seek it."

5.content: A wealthy merchant who trusted that money could buy anything. He bought traitors to kill the Seahook boss, oil to burn the evidence and intel from a "mysterious businesswoman". Jahoda, barely past childhood, hunted him alone. She raided his camp night after night until rumours called her a ghost or a member of the Wild Hunt. At last, gaunt and fevered, she walked into his torchlit trap. He offered her anything; she killed him. She survived with terrible wounds and an empty right sleeve, owing Nefer a debt she paid with her labour.

6.comment: Jahoda: The Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau infiltration
6.content: Jahoda's first big job with the Traveler (6.0). Lauma wanted the Curatorium's help to get into the Fatui facility after Moon Marrow. Nefer, unusually polite, pressed Jahoda into saying yes, then fired her "effective immediately" until the job was done. Jahoda tried to skip the meeting, but Lauma's Sniffer Mole found her. She used an ID card stolen from a drunk Fatuus at the Flagship, which turned out to belong to a maintenance intern. After a grate separated her from the others, she guided them by terminal and hijacked bots. Then she stole a high-level card and drew off the guards with an alarm. When things went too far, she insisted on coming down with them.
